deities: Lord Shiva (as Vaidyanath/Baidyanath, the 'Lord of Physicians')
Goddess Parvati (Jayadurga - Shakti Peetha; Sati's heart is believed to have fallen here)
festivals: Shravani Mela (entire Shravan month, July-August - Kanwar Yatra; 50 lakh to 1 crore pilgrims per sources)

history.dynasty: Nagavanshi dynasty (original construction attributed to Puran Mal, 8th c., per historical accounts); present structure attributed to Raja Man Singh, 16th century (per Vajiram & Ravi)
history.period: Mythological origins; existing temple medieval-to-early-modern (exact dates vary by source - verify)
history.summary: Baba Baidyanath Dham at Deoghar is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas (listed as the 5th by some sources), the most sacred Shaivite shrine in eastern India, and also a Shakti Peetha (Hriday Peetha - Sati's heart is believed to have fallen here). The temple complex has the main Shiva shrine plus about 21 other temples (Parvati, Ganesha, Brahma, Kalabhairav, Hanuman, Saraswati, Surya, Ram-Lakshman-Janaki, Ganga, Kali, Annapurna, Lakshmi-Narayan), with the Maa Parvati temple tied to the Shiva temple by red sacred threads, and a large Nandi before the sanctum. Mythology: Ravana received a boon to carry a Jyotirlinga to Lanka but set it down at Deoghar, where it permanently lodged. The temple is mentioned in Puranas, Vedas, Mahabharata and Ramayana (per Vajiram & Ravi). Built in Nagara style with a tall shikhara and large mandapa. NOTE ON RIVAL CLAIMS (as briefed): the Jyotirlinga identity is also claimed by Parli Vaijnath in Maharashtra and Vaijnath (Baijnath) in Himachal Pradesh; this entry documents Deoghar as the CSV intends. The Shravani Mela, with the 100+ km kanwar yatra of Ganga water from Sultanganj, is one of India's largest religious gatherings.

name: Baidyanath Temple (Baba Baidyanath Dham)
town_description: Deoghar, in the Santhal Pargana region of Jharkhand, is one of Hinduism's major pilgrimage cities, centred on the Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga temple. The town's economy and calendar revolve around the temple, especially during the month-long Shravani Mela.
tradition: Shaivism (also a Shakti Peetha - Hriday Peetha)

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport (DED), ~12 km from the temple, with flights from Delhi, Kolkata, Patna and Ranchi (per panchang.org - verify schedules).
travel.railway: Jasidih Junction, ~7 km from the temple, is the nearest major railhead; Deoghar and Baba Baidyanath Dham stations also serve the town (verify).
travel.road: Well connected by road to Patna, Ranchi, Asansol and Bhagalpur (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: December to February for pleasant weather (per travel guides); Shravan (July-August) for the mela - extremely crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM-3:30 PM and 6:00 PM-9:00 PM (multiple sources); morning aarti ~4:00-4:30 AM, evening aarti ~6:00 PM. Special near-round-the-clock timings apply during Shravan (verify locally).
